Autoresearch

Turn Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, pi, or Muse into an engine that won't stop improving.

Karpathy's autoresearch, in one line: constraint plus a mechanical metric plus autonomous iteration equals compounding gains.

"Set the GOAL → The agent runs the LOOP → You wake up to results"

You don't need AGI. You need a goal, a metric, and a loop that never quits.

The core skill, bundled runtime, installation, and verification run on Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, pi, and Muse. Hook guardrails ship for Claude Code (native hooks) and pi (extension events).

Fork-and-flush: metric loops escape plateaus the way Cai et al. (arXiv:2610.07447) do. At 33% and 66% of the budget, or after 5 iterations with no keep, the loop forks fresh-context branches from the best commit so far, runs each briefly, and keeps the winner. Half the branches pick their own ideas (randomness); the other half each get a distinct experiment from a stateless Advisor that reads the results log (Zhang et al., arXiv:2610.07625); Guided: R sets the split. The orchestrator answers a plateau with FORK before it gives up. See guide/autoresearch.md.

Bumblebee collects inventory. It reads package, extension, and developer-tool metadata on macOS and Linux developer endpoints, and it does not write to them.

It answers one narrow supply-chain question: an advisory names a package, extension, or version. Which developer machines show a match in their on-disk metadata right now?

SBOMs tell you what shipped. EDR tells you what ran or touched the network. Supply-chain response usually needs a third view, and it is a messy one: lockfiles, package-manager metadata, extension manifests, developer-tool configs, all sitting in whatever state each machine left them.

Bumblebee reads that scattered state and turns it into structured NDJSON component records. Hand it an exposure catalog and it flags exact matches. If you already know what you are looking for, that gives you a fast, read-only exposure check.

SkillsBench tests whether AI agents can use Skills to do professional work across many domains. It measures one thing: how much better a model gets at complex real-world tasks when you hand it specialized Skills.

Production environments don't install one Skill. They install hundreds. So we rebuilt SkillsBench to match. The original gave each task only the Skill tied to it. Ours drops every task into a global environment holding all 195 specialized Skills. Nothing else changes. Now the question is whether an agent can find the right Skills in that pile, pick them, and string them into a workflow that finishes the job.

We benchmarked vibeskills v4.1.0 on SkillsBench with DeepSeekV4Flash-VE and OpenHands as the baseline setup. Against the baseline without vibeskills, vibeskills lifted the mean verifier reward by 21.12 percentage points, used 29.6% fewer tokens, and made 33.1% fewer tool calls.

sem is a semantic version control tool that works on top of Git. It parses your code with tree-sitter, extracts every function, class, and method as an entity, and diffs at the entity level instead of lines. So you see "function blahh was modified" instead of "lines x-y changed."

It works in any Git repo with no setup.

IWE: a Markdown knowledge base you and your AI agent work on together

Your notes are your agent's memory. IWE is where you work on them together.

Most AI conversations start from zero. You explain your project, your decisions, your reasoning. Next session, you explain it all again. Your own notes sit somewhere else, out of the agent's reach.

Or the agent "remembers" something in its internal memory, and you can't see what it saved or fix what it got wrong. That memory doesn't follow you to the other agents you work with.

IWE gives you and your AI agents one shared place to work, right inside your project: a folder of connected Markdown documents. Specs, plans, decisions. Keep your own ideas there. Ask your agent to save what you learn together. Come back to that context as your work grows. You can read, edit, and organize those documents yourself, and they stay yours.
